Title: Takiyuddin refuses to withdraw 'munafik' remark, proposes mediation
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan has written to the Dewan Rakyat speaker proposing mediation to resolve the controversy over his use of the word "munafik" (hypocrite) in Parliament.
Takiyuddin, who is the Kota Baru MP, said he had not withdrawn the remark but had instead proposed mediation as an amicable way to resolve the issue.
"I have not withdrawn it. Instead, I wrote to the speaker proposing that he convene a mediation session.
"The speaker would call Jelutong MP RSN Rayer and me in for a discussion to try to resolve the matter," he told a press conference after the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (HIMPAK) gathering last night.
Takiyuddin said the speaker's office had received the letter on Thursday.
"Thursday was supposed to be the deadline, so I sent the letter, which has been received.
"I am now waiting for the speaker's response on whether the proposed mediation will proceed.
"If mediation does not take place, I may be referred to the Committee of Privileges," he said.
Also present were Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang and his deputy, Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man.
It was reported that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul had instructed
Takiyuddin
to withdraw the word 'munafik', which he used while debating the 2027 Budget last week.
He said Takiyuddin could withdraw the remark either in the Dewan Rakyat or by writing to the speaker.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor Sultan: Monarchy remains a pillar of stability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Although society has evolved, the fundamental role of a constitutional monarch remains unchanged, the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, said.
His Royal Highness said the Ruler had a responsibility to uphold the Constitution, preserve continuity and serve as a symbol of unity above political differences.
"The monarchy provides stability during times of change and reminds us that enduring institutions continue to play an important role in safeguarding national harmony," he said in a special interview in conjunction with his 25 years on the Selangor throne.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the Constitution provided clear guidance on his responsibilities.
"My responsibility is to serve all the people of Selangor without favour or prejudice," he said.
His Royal Highness noted that respect for constitutional principles, impartiality and fairness enabled the monarchy to remain a trusted institution for all citizens, regardless of their background or political beliefs.
The monarchy, he said, represented continuity, stability, service and responsibility.
"It reminds us that leadership carries obligations rather than privileges," His Highness said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said these values remained relevant because societies benefited from institutions that encouraged moderation, unity and respect for the rule of law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor's strength lies in its people, says Sultan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan of Selangor has credited the people of the state for making his 25 years as ruler a successful and meaningful journey.
His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said Selangor had remained one of the country's most important states, thanks to the contributions of its people and those who had made it their home.
"This would not have been possible without the role of Selangorians and the millions from other states who work here and make Selangor their home.
"I am thankful and proud to have been the ruler of this state over the past 25 years and Raja Muda for 33 years," he said, expressing gratitude to Allah for granting him good health.
Reflecting on his reign, Sultan Sharafuddin said every year had brought its own challenges and blessings, but the most meaningful moments had been those spent meeting the people of Selangor, celebrating their successes and standing alongside them during difficult times.
"I have witnessed our state continue to grow into one of the nation's leading centres of commerce, education and innovation, while maintaining its cultural and religious heritage," he said in an interview in conjunction with his Silver Jubilee celebrations.
His Royal Highness said he treasured seeing young people of all races excel, communities unite in times of adversity, and institutions work together for the betterment of society.
"These are reminders that the true strength of Selangor lies not only in its economy but also in its people," he said.
Asked how his understanding of leadership had evolved since ascending the throne, Sultan Sharafuddin said leadership was ultimately about responsibility and service.
"Over the years, I have come to appreciate even more deeply that a ruler must listen carefully before making judgments, remain calm during uncertainty, and always place the interests of the people above all else.
"Experience has taught me that leadership requires consistency, patience and humility. A ruler's responsibility is not merely to respond to the present but also to safeguard the future for generations to come," he said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said Selangor had continued to strengthen its position as Malaysia's economic engine while expanding opportunities in education, healthcare, infrastructure and investment.
"But we must not rest on our laurels. Other states, such as Johor and Penang, have become competitors too, but that is good and healthy," he said.
However, he expressed dissatisfaction that basic problems, particularly flooding and cleanliness, remained unresolved.
"Simple matters like floods and cleanliness remain unresolved, which makes me unhappy," he said, adding that he continued to receive complaints about poor rubbish collection, inadequate maintenance of cleanliness and flooding.
The ruler said the public often sent him complaints directly, complete with their personal details and photographs, which he would then forward to the menteri besar's office.
Sultan Sharafuddin said preserving harmony among Selangor's diverse communities was equally important.
"Economic success is meaningful only when it translates into better lives for ordinary citizens. Progress should always be measured not simply by numbers, but by the well-being, dignity and opportunities enjoyed by the people," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seremban records highest API reading at 169
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seremban recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 169 as of 8am today, with unhealthy air quality also recorded in several other areas.
Bandaraya Melaka recorded an API reading of 163, while Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Bukit Rambai in Melaka registered 162 each.
Batu Pahat and Pasir Gudang in Johor also recorded 162, while Tangkak registered 161.
Other areas with unhealthy air quality included Kluang (158), Alor Gajah and Pengerang (156 each), Segamat (155), IPD Serian in Sarawak (153), Cheras in Kuala Lumpur, Port Dickson in Negri Sembilan and Sri Aman in Sarawak (152 each), and Putrajaya and Kapit in Sarawak (151 each).
Petaling Jaya and Klang in Selangor recorded API readings of 133 and 121 respectively.
Meanwhile, Langkawi in Kedah recorded an API reading of 50, followed by Kangar in Perlis (48), Kota Baru in Kelantan (45), Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu (44), Tanah Merah in Kelantan (39) and Besut in Terengganu (25).
The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) also reported moderate air quality at 41 monitoring stations nationwide.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor Sultan urges youths to stay united and informed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan of Selangor hopes future generations of Selangorians will be knowledgeable, compassionate, resilient, united and respectful of others.
His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said young people should strive for excellence without losing their sense of responsibility towards society.
"They should also understand that diversity is one of Malaysia's greatest strengths. Mutual respect and understanding will remain essential to our continued harmony and progress," he said in a special interview held in conjunction with his Silver Jubilee celebrations.
The Selangor ruler also advised young people to read news reports in depth before commenting, particularly on social media, rather than forming opinions based solely on headlines.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the younger generation had rightly placed importance on environmental sustainability and heritage preservation.
"Economic progress should never come at the expense of our natural environment or historical identity.
"Planning for future generations means protecting forests, rivers and green spaces while preserving our historical landmarks and cultural traditions. Development and conservation are not opposing goals; they should reinforce one another," he said.
His Royal Highness also noted that education remained the foundation of long-term progress, particularly in preparing young people for a rapidly changing world.
"Artificial intelligence may not replace all jobs, but in many instances, people who are trained in AI will replace those who are not.
"Selangor must not lose out in this area. We must be ready for this, and I hope the state government realises it," he said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also cautioned that the well-being of senior citizens must not be overlooked as Selangor moves towards becoming an ageing society.
The Sultan said healthcare services must evolve alongside demographic changes, while innovation should continue to strengthen the state's competitiveness.
His Royal Highness proposed that Selangor strive to become the first state to establish a dedicated geriatric medical centre specialising in the health, care, prevention and treatment of conditions affecting older adults.
These include age-related problems such as falls, frailty, urinary incontinence and memory decline.
"We need to prioritise the overall quality of life of the elderly, including their safety, independence and balanced medication," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN-BN seat allocation for Melaka polls based on incumbency
Article:
KOTA BARU: The seat allocation between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election will be based on the incumbent concept.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the concept had been generally agreed upon by all component parties in the coalition.
"The concept that has been generally agreed upon is 'incumbent', meaning the sitting representative.
"This approach is the same as that used in other states previously.
"In Kelantan, Pas and Perikatan Nasional (PN) hold 42 of the 45 seats, making them the incumbents. In Terengganu, Pas and PN are the incumbents in all 28 seats," he said at a press conference after the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (HIMPAK) gathering last night.
He said Umno was also the incumbent in 21 seats in Melaka.
"In Melaka, Umno is the incumbent in 21 seats. So, we have to understand it that way," he said.
Also present were Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang and his deputy, Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was reported as saying that
negotiations with Pas
for the Melaka state election had been finalised.
He said BN would contest 21 state seats, while Pas and its allies would contest the remaining seven.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: 'Honk twice to congratulate me': First-car celebration goes viral
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A cheeky note on a man's first car turned an ordinary drive in Segamat, Johor, into a moment of celebration when a truck driver behind him honked twice to congratulate him.
"I bought a new car. Honk twice to congratulate me," read the message on the vehicle, which was filmed travelling along a road in Segamat.
The truck driver duly obliged, giving the man and his colleagues the reaction they had hoped for.
The clip,
shared by Threads user
@alfiqzareeq_, has garnered more than 1.1 million views and 36,000 likes.
In the comments, the user revealed that the car belonged to a colleague whose first vehicle purchase had prompted an office-wide celebration.
"The whole office came to celebrate delivery day. The surprise honking sign, flower garland and posters were all our colleagues' ideas," he wrote.
Another video shared in the comments showed colleagues documenting the occasion, from the owner signing the purchase paperwork to trying out his new car.
"Thank you to everyone who joined us in celebrating our friend getting his first car. This will motivate him to work harder to earn a living," the user added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen dies, five injured as car crashes into tree
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 16-year-old teenager was killed while five others were injured after the car they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a tree near a surau in Kampung Jalan Baru, Simpang Lima, last night.
Batu Pahat Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Zulmazi Ariffin said the department received a distress call at 10.16pm and dispatched 13 personnel to the scene along with two Emergency Medical Rescue Services units and a Fire Rescue Tender.
Upon arrival, the operation team found that the Proton Wira carrying six people had skidded and crashed into the tree.
"The victims comprised two adult men, two adult women and two boys. One of the victims, identified as Putera Muhaimin Qudrat Mohd Noor Wandi, 16, was pronounced dead at the scene.
"The five other victims, Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis Mohd Noor Wandi, 15; Nor Azlan Shaharudin, 27; Putera Khairunas Mohd Noor Wandi, 11; Putera Aidin Firdaus Mohd Noor Wandi, three; and Rahmah A Rahim, 26; were injured and taken to hospital for treatment," he said in a statement today.

Title: Malaysia-origin vessel seized in Indonesia with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities seized 1.16 tonnes of ketamine from a Mongolian-flagged vessel that had sailed from Malaysia in the waters off North Sumatra province earlier this week, national police chief Suyudi Ario Seto said on Friday.
Indonesian authorities, including the police and customs office, intercepted the tanker in the waters off Tanjung Balai in the province earlier this week, Seto said.
They arrested seven Indonesians and one Taiwanese national, including the captain, engineers and an oiler, he said.
The ketamine was found in 58 sacks weighing a total of 1.16 tonnes, Seto said. He added that the haul had a street value of 3.48 trillion rupiah (US$192.64 million).
[[nid:1562346]]
The tanker departed from Pasir Gudang in Malaysia, transited through the Malacca Strait and headed towards the Andaman Sea, where authorities believe it conducted a ship-to-ship transfer to receive the ketamine.
Authorities had detected 'anomalies' in the vessel's Automatic Identification System before intercepting it, Seto said.
The quantity of drugs demonstrated how destructive "international syndicates are to our national security", he added.
Later on Friday, Seto said authorities in the Indonesian province of Aceh had found 1.2 tonnes of methamphetamine, worth about 2.16 trillion rupiah, at a clandestine laboratory.
Indonesia has strict drug laws and in 2015 executed two Australians from the 'Bali Nine' drug ring for attempting to smuggle heroin out of the resort island of Bali.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pentagon designates Confucius Institutes in US a national security threat
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Defence Department has designated Chinese-funded cultural centres on university campuses known as Confucius Institutes as a threat to US national security, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday.
Washington has long accused Confucius Institutes of being Chinese propaganda tools and has taken steps to crack down on them.
Hegseth, in a video posted on social media, alleged that Confucius Institutes were operating under disguise at US universities and that the Pentagon had added them to its list of institutions that threaten US national security.
"It turns out that 80 new propaganda cells across 30 universities had popped up using different names and different charters, but with the same mission: To steal intellectual property and to infiltrate the minds of American students," Hegseth said.
The Defence Department had "systematically dismantled every single one of these organisations" over the past two months, he said.
The Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Argentine judge dismisses case against Milei over alleged crypto scam
Article:
BUENOS AIRES: A federal judge on Friday dismissed a criminal case against Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister, in which they were accused of promoting a suspected cryptocurrency scam that resulted in at least US$100 million in losses for investors.
"The reported events do not constitute a criminal offence," Judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi said in a ruling reviewed by AFP.
Milei had hailed the $LIBRA meme coin in a social media post in February 2025, saying: "The world wants to invest in Argentina. $LIBRA."
He deleted the post hours later after the currency crashed. Milei later denied promoting the virtual currency, saying he "did not know the details of the project".
Industry experts have called the operation a "rug pull" — a scam in which developers unveil a crypto token, attract investors and then quickly cash out.
The investigation sought to determine whether a coordinated scheme had taken place, with the president's involvement.
Nine other individuals under investigation were also cleared.
The judge wrote that investor losses and the rise and fall in the currency's price were insufficient to establish fraud.
Investigators also found no proof that Karina Milei, the president's right-hand woman who serves as secretary-general of the presidency, had received payments for facilitating meetings between the entrepreneurs behind the virtual currency and her brother.
"Facilitating a contact or helping to organise a meeting does not, in itself, amount to influence peddling," the judge wrote.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea's Kim calls for 'military revolution' as he urges stronger army units
Article:
SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for the country's army companies to be turned into elite, self-sufficient combat units during a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media KCNA said on Saturday.
The event underscored Kim's consistent policy priority of strengthening the military.
In a speech at a conference of company commanders for North Korea's army on Oct 22-23, which KCNA said was the first military-wide gathering since the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, Kim called for every company to be fully prepared so that "the goal of the new-era military build-up" could be achieved.
"Let us build the strongest army and speed up a military revolution in our style," Kim said.
During the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, which sets the country's direction for the next five years, Kim called for stronger conventional armed forces while reaffirming efforts to develop nuclear weapons and missiles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Death in custody: No internal injuries found in post-mortem, 78 quizzed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A post-mortem on a 42-year-old man who died in police custody found no internal organ injuries, although several external injuries were detected.
Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid said the cause of death remained
pending laboratory analysis
.
The man, who was arrested by Cheras police on Sept 19 in connection with investigations under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and Sections 457 and 379 of the Penal Code, was referred to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz on Sept 30 for treatment.
He was given initial treatment by doctors but was pronounced dead at 1.52am on Oct 1.
Aida said the case had been classified as sudden death, with the Death in Custody Criminal Investigation Unit continuing investigations from various angles.
She said the unit had recorded statements from 78 witnesses, including policemen, the public, medical officers, forensic medical specialists, National Legal Aid Foundation representatives and two family members of the deceased.
The case had also been referred to the Independent Police Conduct Commission in accordance with Section 26 of the IPCC Act 2022.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH faces uphill battle, but surprise remains possible [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  DAP and Pakatan Harapan are expected to face an uphill battle in the Melaka polls as a potential Barisan Nasional-Pas electoral pact could consolidate Malay support and replicate the electoral trend seen in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
But political analysts said DAP and PH could still pull off a surprise by winning over young and undecided voters, particularly in mixed constituencies and seats won with narrow margins.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said PH was likely to retain support in five Chinese-majority and mixed-demographic constituencies.
He said support among Chinese and Indian voters, as well as middle-class Malays in urban and semi-urban areas, would be crucial to PH's electoral performance.
"Fundamentally, rural Malay voters remain deeply committed to the Malay-Muslim narrative.
"Conversely, urban Malays and non-Malay voters, particularly the Chinese, prioritise issues such as the cost of living, governance, development and national-level concerns."
He said several national political controversies could influence voter sentiment, including issues involving Tabung Haji, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's donation issue, the political and royal crisis in Negri Sembilan and financial leakages during BN's past administration.
He said these issues could influence young and undecided voters, potentially benefiting PH if they shift support to the coalition.
Despite PH's potential to gain ground, Mazlan said the Malay-Muslim narrative was expected to remain influential among rural Malay voters, giving BN and Pas an advantage in a substantial number of constituencies.
"On paper, BN could win easily. However, in mixed constituencies or areas with narrow margins, the situation could shift, potentially leading to surprises in this state election."
Social media campaigning and the ability to address voters' concerns would be crucial in determining the outcome, he added.
"The party that succeeds in mastering social media and effectively addressing key issues will stand a better chance of winning more seats."
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said PH had a realistic opportunity to spring a surprise in Melaka.
"The BN-Pas electoral understanding gives them a significant advantage in terms of grassroots machinery, Malay voter support and electoral momentum.
"But cooperation does not automatically guarantee a complete transfer of votes between their supporters."
He said PH needed to consolidate its traditional support while attracting undecided and moderate voters, particularly in marginal and mixed constituencies.
"A surprise is possible, but it would require PH to translate dissatisfaction with the political status quo into meaningful gains."
He added that young and undecided voters could play an important role, especially in closely contested seats.
"Issues such as the cost of living, employment opportunities, housing affordability and government accountability could influence their decisions."
He said dissatisfaction with economic conditions would not automatically translate into support for PH, as some voters could hold the coalition accountable for unresolved challenges in its role in the federal government.
He said PH should prioritise competitive constituencies, such as Pengkalan Batu and Duyong, while defending Ayer Keroh, Bukit Katil, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, which it won in 2021.
PH's challenge in rural Malay constituencies was to overcome the perception that BN and Pas better represent Malay-Muslim interests, he added.
"PH should focus on economic security, rural development, agricultural assistance and equitable governance, while strengthening the credibility of Malay leaders from PKR and Amanah. Protecting Malay-Muslim interests and maintaining Malaysia's multiracial political framework are not mutually exclusive."
The Election Commission has set Nov 10 for nomination day, Nov 14 for polling day and Oct 31 for early voting.
Melaka has 28 state seats, with a simple majority requiring at least 15 seats and a two-thirds majority requiring 19 seats.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN won 21 seats, allowing it to form the state government. PH won five seats, four of which went to DAP, while Perikatan Nasional secured two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Judge puts off decision on Charlie Kirk murder trial date
Article:
NEW MEXICO: A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk more than a year ago, media reported.
At a hearing in Provo, Utah, District Court Judge Tony Graf heard arguments from defence lawyers, prosecutors and a lawyer for Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, before saying he needed to consider their positions. He set a new hearing for November 9, television station KUTV reported.
Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to seven counts, including aggravated murder, for allegedly shooting Kirk as he held one of his trademark debates at Utah Valley University in Orem. Robinson's lawyers expect a six-to-seven-month trial.
Robinson's attorneys had asked for a trial in late 2029 to give them time to challenge Utah's request for the death penalty, gather additional evidence and seek a change of venue, among other issues, according to a scheduling memo.
Prosecutors, meanwhile, sought a date of Jan 31, 2028, to start what they expect to be a 17-week trial, according to their scheduling memo.
In a separate filing, Erika Kirk said the defence request was "grossly out of line with comparable cases" and requested that the trial start no later than Oct 4, 2027.
Shortly before Friday's hearing, President Donald Trump, with whom Kirk had been allied, criticised Graf's handling of the case in a social media post, saying it should be tried within a month and that Graf was asking "questions that people already know the answer to".
Kirk was a polarising figure in US politics. He was admired by conservatives for mobilising young voters around his Christian and right-wing views. Opponents criticised his rhetoric on immigration, race, gender and other social issues.
Prosecutors allege Robinson targeted Kirk because of his opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights.
Defence attorney Richard Novak has said Kirk spoke "hatefully" about people who did not have traditional gender identities or were not heterosexual, but there was no evidence Robinson opposed those views.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants want clarity over Waze ban
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   Civil servants are seeking clarity over the decision to ban them from using the Waze navigation application. This   includes  the government's concerns over  the app's alleged links to Israel and the security of users' location data.
A civil servant, who spoke on condition of anonymity,  asked why the ban was not extended to all users if the government was concerned that location data could be exposed to the Israeli government or companies.
"Ordinary Malaysians are also using Waze and their location data could be exposed, too. If it is a security threat to the country, then it should be a blanket ban.
"But if the concern is only about government operations, the government should explain why the restriction is necessary for all civil servants," he said.
He added that if the Waze ban was on national security grounds, then it should focus only on sensitive government bodies, including the Prime Minister's Office, Home Ministry and  Defence Ministry.
"Their movements and activities may involve sensitive matters, so there is a stronger reason to take precautions there."
He said it was unfair to single out civil servants as the app was still available for use by other Malaysians.
On Wednesday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered civil servants to stop using Waze over concerns that sensitive government information and personal data could be exploited by Israel.
However, Anwar said yesterday the government had not ruled out imposing a nationwide ban on Waze once suitable alternatives became available.
"I will not allow civil servants to use it under any circumstances. Waze is banned.
"We need to study the available alternatives. If we find that their capabilities are sufficiently developed, we may consider using the facilities available."
Anwar said Malaysians should switch to locally developed alternatives such as TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, citing assurances over data security and personal information protection.
Another civil servant asked why United States-based apps such as Google Maps, Instagram and WhatsApp remained accessible.
"Why is Waze banned while Google Maps is available? Both are used for navigation and require location data."
She added that Instagram and WhatsApp should also be considered when the government assessed the potential exposure of personal information to foreign companies.
"If the concern is about foreign companies collecting data, then the government needs to explain the criteria it uses.
"Otherwise, people will question why one application is banned while other widely used apps remain accessible."
Another civil servant questioned whether disciplinary action would be taken if a civil servant was found using Waze.
"We are expected to follow government instructions, but there must also be a clear explanation why this decision was made. If the concern is national security, then explain to us what the concern is and why Waze is singled out," she said.
Civil servants have been warned that they would face disciplinary action if found using the app, with department heads overseeing compliance with the directive.
Asked whether any spot checks had been conducted in her department, she said: "So far, there have been no checks to see whether we have downloaded TuJu and uninstalled Waze.
"We have received instructions from the top management reminding us to comply with the Waze directive and not make any comments on social media, particularly those that belittle TuJu."
She also questioned whether the government had properly considered the alternatives available to those who rely on Waze for their travel needs, saying her experience with TuJu had raised concerns over its reliability.
"I searched for my home address but the app displayed the message: 'No results found, try searching with different keywords'.
"The same thing happened when I tried searching for Dataran Merdeka. If the app cannot even find this location, how reliable is it as an alternative to Waze?"
She said navigation apps were not just about finding the direction to a destination, but also providing accurate locations and convenient routes, particularly for those unfamiliar with an area.
She added that civil servants  would need an alternative that could meet their daily needs, including travelling to meetings, attending official functions and finding unfamiliar addresses.
"If we are told to stop using Waze immediately, then the alternative should at least work properly.
"Otherwise, it will be difficult for users who depend on navigation apps to get around."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST COURT WATCH: Shuhaily charged, Teresa Kok wins suit, Jovian loses appeal & Papagomo acquitted [WATCH]
Article:
MCBA chief and former Temerloh police chief charged in separate cases
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency director-general
Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain made headlines
after becoming the first high-ranking officer of the agency to be charged with assaulting two Special Branch policemen.
Shuhaily, 54, appeared calm as he faced two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to lance corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, 25, and Mohamad Faiz Saman, 40.
He appeared before magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani at the Sepang court complex, about three weeks after a video allegedly showing him assaulting the duo, who are travel control officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
If convicted under Section 323 of the Penal Code, Shuhaily faces a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
He was released after a family friend posted bail of RM1,500 with one surety for each charge. He is set to return to court for case management on Nov 25.
Below are the other major court cases this week
FORMER TEMERLOH POLICE CHIEF JAILED FOR BRIBERY
On Wednesday, former Temerloh police chief Superintendent Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusoff was
sentenced to eight months in jail
after being found guilty of 46 counts of accepting bribes totalling RM69,600 between 2019 and 2023.
Temerloh Sessions Court judge Sazlina Safie ruled that the 56-year-old failed to raise reasonable doubt over the prosecution's case that he had received the money through online transfers into his bank account over nearly four years and had abused his authority for personal gain.
The court rejected a plea by his lawyer, Datuk M. Athimulan, for a fine instead of jail, arguing that the conviction itself could cost his client his job, pension and other benefits accumulated throughout his 36-years service.
Azhar was granted a stay of execution pending appeal, with the court increasing his bail by RM5,000 to RM30,000.
JOVIAN LOSES APPEALS
On Tuesday, the Court of Appeal dismissed fashion designer
Datuk Jovian Mandagie's
appeals against summary judgments obtained by Bina Pragmatik Sdn Bhd and Cekap Air Sdn Bhd in a 2-1 majority decision.
The ruling upheld the High Court decisions ordering Jovian to repay RM10 million in alleged friendly loans from the two companies, together with RM60,000 in costs.
Judge Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, who chaired the panel, and Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril found that Jovian had failed to provide sufficient evidence to support his claim that the money was intended as business investments rather than loans.
However, dissenting judge Datin Evrol Mariette Peters said the transfer of money into law firms' client accounts did not, in itself, establish that the payments were loans.
She also noted that neither company had produced contemporaneous written documents establishing the alleged loan agreements, while the letters of demand issued to Jovian did not refer to the purported arrangements.
COUPLE SENT TO THE GALLOWS
A couple known as Ah Long Harimau was sentenced to death by the Federal Court for murdering 38-year-old Heng Heow Lin in Sibu, Sarawak in 2020, over a RM800 debt.
Judges Datuk Azizah Nawawi, Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang and Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah unanimously dismissed the final appeal of Seow Pei Chee and her husband Cheung Chia Ming, both 44.
The court heard that the victim was repeatedly abused and strangled before her body was stuffed into luggage and dumped by the roadside over the debt.
The couple had pushed Heng and her daughter into prostitution, kept the earnings and assaulted them when their collection was too little.
TYCOON CLAIMS TRIAL OVER RM10 MILLION CHEATING CHARGES
Businessman
Tan Sri Tan Kean Soon,
63, pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court to four counts of cheating fellow businessman Datuk Seri Keh Chuan Seng, 55, of RM10 million by allegedly misleading him into believing he could resolve issues involving frozen bank accounts and a police investigation linked to money laundering.
Tan allegedly induced Keh to hand over RM2 million, RM3 million, S$1.5 million and RM500,000 through Datuk Seri Chiau Beng Teik.
The charges, under Section 420 of the Penal Code, carry imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Judge Azrul Darus granted Tan bail of RM1 million with one surety, despite the prosecution's objection to bail given the non-bailable nature of the offence and the RM10 million involved.
TERESA KOK WINS DEFAMATION SUIT AGAINST AKMAL, AWARDED RM250,000
Seputeh member of parliament Teresa Kok
won her defamation suit
against Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh at the Melaka High Court on Oct 19 over his remarks aimed at her on the country's halal certification issue.
Judicial Commissioner Datuk Isa Aziz Ibrahim ordered Akmal to pay RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages as well as RM50,000 in costs.
In the 2024 suit, Kok claimed Akmal had defamed her in two articles published on a news portal, titled "Akmal: Saya Minta Kerajaan Sediakan Logo Non-Halal, Tampal Pada Dahi Teresa" and "UMNO Youth Chief swipes at 'old Nyonya' Teresa over halal cert".
The court also ordered Akmal to remove the video from his social media accounts within seven days and permanently restrained him from republishing the defamatory statements or words to the same effect.
PAPAGOMO FREED ONCE AGAIN, A-GC TO APPEAL
Blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, has been
acquitted and discharged
for the second time over alleged remarks that the government was pro-Israel.
The 43-year-old was freed by Sessions Court judge Siti Aminah Ghazali at the end of the defence case on Monday, after she found that the defence had raised reasonable doubt in the prosecution's case.
She had previously freed Wan Azri at the close of the prosecution's case before the High Court remitted the case back to Siti Aminah after ruling that a prima facie had been established.
However, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has decided to appeal against the acquittal, setting the stage for another round of legal proceedings.
He was charged with making the allegedly seditious remarks on the Facebook page of Halid Hamidi at 1pm on Nov 8, 2023.
The charge framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, carries a maximum fine of RM5,000, a jail term of up to three years, or both upon conviction.
LEE ZII JIA SETTLES FAMILY DISPUTE, COMPANY TO HOLD EGM
Professional shuttler
Lee Zii Jia drew attention
at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Tuesday when he appeared for mediation over a family dispute involving his company, LZJ Management Sdn Bhd.
The dispute was resolved through an amicable settlement, with High Court judge Leong Wai Hong recording a consent judgment on Oct 20.
Under the agreement, the company must hold an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Oct 31, with the costs to be borne by the company.
Pending the meeting, Lee's father, Lee Chee Hin, 59, and elder sister, Lee Zii Yii, 30, are restrained from approving or authorising directors' fees, allowances, bonuses or other financial benefits for themselves, apart from their monthly salaries.
They are also barred from making decisions that could materially affect the company's management, administration or control without prior court approval.
Lee, 28, filed the originating summons on July 2, naming LZJ Management, his father, sister and younger brother, Lee Tao, 25, as respondents. The court made no order as to costs, following the settlement between the parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST CRIME WATCH: Murder, school attack and baby's death dominate the week [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Murder, violence, organised crime and shocking attacks dominated Malaysia's crime headlines this week, with several cases drawing widespread public attention and raising concerns over safety and security.
From the murder of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer at a government residential complex in Nilai to an alleged attack on a teacher by a Form Four student at an international school in Kuching, the cases highlighted the range and severity of crimes being investigated by police.
Here are some of the cases that made headlines this week:
MCBA officer found dead at quarters, husband remanded
The murder of MCBA officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, remained one of the week's most closely followed cases after she was found dead at a government residential complex in Nilai on Oct 15.
A post-mortem found that she died from pressure on the neck, while stab wounds were also detected on the side of her abdomen and cheek.
Her husband, in his 30s, was detained after surrendering at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang.
Police have recorded statements from 18 people to assist investigations.
The suspect was remanded for seven days to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Police also revealed that the suspect had 16 previous criminal records, including 10 involving narcotics offences and six relating to housebreaking, theft and possession of stolen property.
Student attacks teacher with axe at Kuching school
A 16-year-old Form Four student was arrested after
attacking a female teacher
at an international school in Kuching on Wednesday.
The incident occurred at 7.49am, with police confirming that the teacher suffered an injury to her hand.
Police seized an axe and a penknife at the scene, while reports also stated that the student had brought firecrackers to the school.
The incident quickly went viral after footage purportedly showing the attack circulated online, prompting renewed concerns over the safety of teachers and students.
School authorities said the student was restrained following the incident before police were alerted.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, including the motive for the attack.
Geng Suria linked to 20 violent and property crimes busted
Bukit Aman announced they had busted an
organised crime group
known as Geng Suria, which is believed to be linked to 20 property and violent crimes in Kedah.
Federal police Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the group was believed to have been active since early 2024 and comprised nine members aged between 28 and 52.
The group was allegedly led by a 30-year-old local man and targeted homes belonging to foreigners, business premises and residential properties identified by its leader.
Police said members used dangerous weapons, including knives and machetes, during robberies and did not hesitate to injure victims.
Several victims allegedly suffered serious injuries, while the group was believed to have caused losses amounting to hundreds of thousands of ringgit.
The operation, dubbed Op Sunset, was conducted by Bukit Aman CID with the Kedah contingent CID from Sept 24 to 27 in Kedah and Perak.
Six suspects were arrested, while three others were already being held at prisons in Sungai Buloh, Pokok Sena and Sungai Petani for other offences.
The nine are scheduled to be charged soon at the Sungai Petani Sessions Court for membership in an organised crime group.
Baby dies after suffering head injuries from blunt-force trauma
The death of a 10-month-old boy in Tasek Gelugor, Penang, took a more serious turn after a
post-mortem found
that he had suffered head injuries consistent with blunt-force trauma.
The baby was under the care of a babysitter when he was found weak and lethargic at her home on Monday morning.
The babysitter reportedly discovered the child at 9.50am before he was taken for medical treatment.
He later died, prompting police to detain the babysitter to assist investigations.
The post-mortem found that the injuries could have been fatal.
Police are continuing investigations to determine how the injuries occurred and whether a criminal element was involved.
13 held over Molotov cocktail attack on Rohingya settlement
Police arrested 13 local men, aged between 16 and 31, over an alleged Molotov cocktail attack on a Rohingya settlement in Kulai Besar, Johor.
The suspects were arrested in and around Johor Baru during a five-day operation conducted by the Johor CID between Oct 13 and 18.
Four of the suspects were found to have a combined 12 previous criminal and drug-related offences.
The attack occurred on Oct 13, when Molotov cocktails were allegedly thrown at the settlement.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack and the motive behind it.
Cross-border operation cripples online vice syndicate
A joint Malaysia-Singapore operation resulted in the arrest of 30 people over an alleged
cross-border prostitution syndicate
that used Malaysia as its base to offer online sex services to customers in Singapore.
The operation involved Bukit Aman and the Singapore Police Force, with raids conducted to dismantle the syndicate's operations.
Police said the group was believed to have used websites to advertise prostitution services to customers in Singapore.
Nine people wanted by Singapore police over their alleged involvement in the syndicate were also arrested in Malaysia.
The operation highlighted cross-border organised vice activities, particularly by using online platforms and exploiting the close movement of people between Malaysia and Singapore.
Investigations are continuing to establish the full structure of the syndicate and the respective roles of those detained.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rubio calls for Cubans to work with CIA, but warns: Be 'discreet'
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday urged Cubans to make "discreet" contact with American intelligence services as Washington seeks to force an end to the island's communist government.
For months, President Donald Trump and other senior US officials have openly hinted at a military intervention or takeover of Cuba, ramping up economic, political and legal pressure on the country.
"To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba – now is the time," Rubio said on social media.
"The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discreet partnership with the CIA."
Trump, speaking at a midterm rally in Florida earlier on Friday, underlined his ambitions to impose regime change in Cuba.
"Those beautiful (military) ships will pass Cuba. We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands. And then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal."
In the latest US move against the Cuban leadership, Florida's top prosecutor this week announced an arrest warrant for former president Raul Castro on state murder charges that echo a federal indictment unveiled earlier this year.
[[nid:1562313]]
Castro, 95, is wanted on murder charges connected to the 1996 shooting down of two civilian aircraft belonging to "Brothers to the Rescue", an organisation assisting Cubans fleeing to the US state by sea.
Castro, brother of the late revolutionary leader and US nemesis Fidel Castro, was indicted on federal charges related to the incident in May.
Trump previously seized on a US indictment to justify military action that toppled Venezuela's then-president Nicolas Maduro, a staunch ally of the Cuban authorities.
Current Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel has said the US federal indictment against Castro has "no legal basis" and was an attempt "to justify the folly of a military aggression against Cuba".
Washington also imposed a de facto energy blockade on Cuba in January, threatening to sanction any country that supplies fuel to the island of 9.4 million people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump ends tariffs on some Canadian products, aiming to help Senator Collins
Article:
WASHINGTON: With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight re-election battle, President Donald Trump signed an order on Friday to remove 50 per cent tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit companies in the state.
The Republican president's hefty tariffs on Canada have caused friction with the US neighbour to the north while creating problems for American businesses in Maine and other states that rely on certain Canadian goods.
With the Nov 3 US midterm elections looming and Republicans fighting to retain control of Congress, Senator Susan Collins had urged the White House to address tariffs on products affecting Maine companies and farmers.
Trump's order exempted plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, packing crates and boxes, as well as fresh and dried seaweed, the White House said.
The changes take effect on Oct 30, four days before the election.
Trump added a number of Canadian products to the 50 per cent tariff list to offset the tariff relief provided in his order, including carpets, paints, shampoos, cocoa powder, wooden coffins, ice cream sticks, air-conditioning machines, chest freezers, archery equipment and canoes.
Collins said the relief would aid Maine's blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers.
"These producers are a vital part of our state's economy and support our rural and coastal communities," Collins said. "Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialised equipment, packaging materials and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."
Democrat Troy Jackson is seeking to oust Collins in next month's election in a race that polls indicate is very close. The two sparred over tariffs at an Oct 6 debate.
"Trump's trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers," Jackson said on Friday after Trump's action. "Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire."
Trump imposed 50 per cent tariffs on US$20 billion of Canadian imports in August, which took effect after talks between the two countries collapsed. Canada retaliated in September with tariffs ranging from 15 per cent to 50 per cent on US$20 billion in US goods.
Canada and the United States have been engaged in a standoff over the tariffs since Trump imposed them. Trump asserted on Friday that Canada was working on a deal.
Republican candidates in northern US border states most affected by the tariffs, including Maine and Michigan, are trying to strike a balance between appealing to Trump's loyal conservative base and winning over independent voters.
'Refining the scope'
In a statement concerning Trump's action on Friday, White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said the president "continues to address Canada's discriminatory treatment of US commerce" and that the new moves were "further refining the scope" of the previously announced tariffs.
The Canadian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The economies of Michigan and Maine have long been intertwined with that of Canada, covering everything from auto parts to lumber to fruit-picking equipment.
Republicans may need to win closely contested Senate races in both states to maintain their majority in the chamber.
"Trump's desperate, 11th-hour attempt to save Susan Collins' political career is an admission that American voters are rejecting his toxic tariff policies.
"No one will forget how Trump raised prices on thousands of products American families need by slapping trade taxes on goods from around the world," Senator Ron Wyden, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, said in a statement on Friday.
Trump's threat in September to block Canadian jet maker Bombardier from the US market became a political issue in Kansas, where the company employs 1,500 workers in Wichita. T
rump dropped the threatened ban this week after calls from Kansas lawmakers, including Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is also locked in a tough re-election race.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Protests expected in Rome, Milan under heavy security
Article:
ROME: Security forces are deploying in large numbers across Italy on Saturday for protests planned in eight cities, including Rome and Milan, after some demonstrations turned violent last weekend.
The demonstrations come amid a wave of protests by students, truck drivers and farmers over budget cuts and cost-of-living issues such as housing and fuel prices.
Rome's police force said in a statement it would "saturate both physical and virtual territory" and use drones and helicopters to monitor the demonstrations.
It said it still "aimed to safeguard the full exercise of the right to express one's views, including dissent, but strictly in compliance with the law".
In Milan, extra soldiers deployed following last weekend's protests will patrol the city centre, but Mayor Giuseppe Sala said there were no plans to shut down the city.
"Last weekend there weren't enough of us. We will simply try to be more numerous," he told Radio Lombardia.
Sala also encouraged shops to remain open on Saturday, after several boutiques in the fashion hub were looted last weekend and others closed or removed their window displays.
"If panic spreads then everything stops," he said on Friday.
A group calling itself the "Oct 17 Movement" has called for protests at 1300 GMT in eight Italian cities.
It said there would be three protests in each city, which would converge at one location, and that the locations would only be revealed half an hour before the start.
[[nid:1562298]]
Separately, an anti-war movement called the "Anti-imperialist Axis" has also organised a rally in Rome.
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's hard-right government adopted a security decree this week that eases detention rules for minors, introduces an offence of "violent participation in a demonstration" and imposes fines on parents for damage caused by their children during protests.
Police said on Friday they had carried out dozens of raids against people suspected of taking part in looting and rioting during last weekend's protests.
The government has also approved a series of measures to help truck drivers and fishermen cope with the spike in fuel prices.
Almost all the truck blockades that had paralysed southern Italy, causing fuel and food shortages for days, have now been lifted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump orders lawsuit to block Alaska Senate result if Republicans lose
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Friday that he had ordered a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to prevent certification of Alaska's Senate election result if the Republican incumbent loses — raising further questions over whether he will accept defeat in the midterms.
"I'm the one that said, 'Do it,'" Trump announced during a trip to Florida, where he is due to cast his own early ballot for the November 3 election to decide control of Congress, currently in Republican hands.
The extraordinary intervention by a president to launch a pre-emptive challenge to a possible election result casts a new shadow over the midterms.
Trump — who tried to overturn the 2020 presidential election after losing to Democrat Joe Biden — has repeatedly questioned the validity of the upcoming election, in which Democrats are forecast to make big gains.
If Democrats win the House of Representatives, as widely expected, they would be able to exert the first real brake on Trump's unprecedented exercise of power since he secured his second term two years ago.
Democrats also have an outside chance of winning the Senate if they can flip a handful of Republican-held seats, including in Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola.
She called the lawsuit "corruption" in a post on X.
Sullivan v Sullivan
In its lawsuit, filed on Thursday, the Justice Department alleged that the presence on the Alaska ballot of a minor additional candidate named Dan J. Sullivan Jr. was part of a deliberate ploy to confuse voters and harm the Republican incumbent's chances.
"The sole purpose of his candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan," the lawsuit said.
Democrats and Sullivan Jr. himself, a registered Republican, have denied this.
The lawsuit asks for certification of a Democratic win to be held up pending an investigation if the Republican incumbent's losing margin is smaller than the number of votes won by his namesake.
Attorney General Todd Blanche, who has repeatedly broken Washington norms about maintaining political distance from the White House, said on Thursday that the Justice Department was not preparing to interfere in the midterms.
But he refused to rule out what he called a "doomsday scenario".
"To say that there's no circumstances that we would ever do that. Of course, I'm not going to say that."
Democrats have accused the Trump administration of seeking ways to steer the results of the November vote by trying to expand federal government control over state-run elections and repeatedly questioning the integrity of results.
Trump won Alaska by 13 percentage points in his 2024 comeback election. But amid growing discontent with Republicans and Trump nationwide, Peltola, a former tribal judge and Alaska Native, is running a strong race.
Alaska is a vast state with a population of just 740,000.
Legal analyst Derek Muller described the Department of Justice's case as "absurdly thin" and unlikely to prevail in court.
"There's essentially no likelihood of success," Muller wrote on the Election Law Blog.
Sullivan Jr. was briefly removed from the ballot this summer but was reinstated by an Alaskan lower court — a decision upheld by the state's supreme court.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
Article:
GENEVA: The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine during the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began on Friday, the head of the World Health Organisation said.
The DR Congo's worst-ever Ebola outbreak has passed the 9,700-case mark, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,600.
Among the many challenges facing the response is the lack of approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the epidemic.
Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will undergo a full-scale human trial in the DRC to determine whether it offers any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.
"Science gives us hope. Today, in Bunia DRC, the first participants were vaccinated in a new Ebola vaccine trial called Tumaini, which means 'hope' in Swahili," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on X.
"This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work.
"In the meantime, the existing Everbo vaccine (licensed for use in preventing other Ebola virus disease) will be tested.
"WHO is supporting this DRC-led effort to find answers and save lives."
The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC — a single trial framework that can test the safety and efficacy of multiple vaccines — should eventually incorporate two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which are undergoing earlier-stage, smaller-scale clinical trials.
One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab being developed by the University of Oxford; the other, by the US-based Moderna group, uses mRNA technology.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore widens haze probe to local firms linked to Indonesian fires
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore expanded on Friday its probe into companies linked to fires in Indonesia, asking 10 locally-based firms for information about their efforts to contain blazes blamed for toxic haze covering the region.
The city-state has beefed up measures to combat the months-long blazes and had vowed legal action against companies responsible for the fires that have made regional air quality among the world's worst.
Over the past week, Singapore issued notices to 10 foreign-based companies, insisting that they deploy fire fighting teams, stop burning or starting new fires in Indonesia and submit information about their links with associated companies in Indonesia and Singapore.
The information is to be reviewed by Singapore's National Environmental Agency (NEA).
In addition to these companies, the NEA is seeking information from 10 Singapore-registered firms in the palm oil or forestry industry who are involved with Indonesian land, the environmental agency said in a statement late Friday.
The information relates to "linkages with associated companies in Singapore and Indonesia, the location of land concessions owned by them as well as fire preventative measures or firefighting efforts", the statement said.
Singapore also said it would form a panel of experts comprising law firms, audit firms and investigative firms with expertise in conducting cross-border inquiries and investigations to help with its probe.
Indonesia experiences fires regularly during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and the draining of peatland for cultivation have rendered previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable.
Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year's blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas.
The fires have raged across forests and peatland, as well as palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms.
Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called "hotspots" in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions.
Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires, including Singapore Exchange-listed First Resources and Singapore-registered Asia Pulp and Paper.
Both are named by the NEA in the latest update on Singapore's probe.
Singapore and Kuala Lumpur again ranked within the world's top 10 most polluted major cities late Friday, according to Swiss-based air monitor IQAir.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taiwan warns of 'destructive winds' as Typhoon Champi batters island
Article:
TAIPEI: A powerful typhoon pounded Taiwan on Friday as authorities warned of "destructive winds" and urged locals to shelter from the storm.
Typhoon Champi dumped heavy rain, toppled trees and knocked out power to thousands of households as it swept past Taiwan's northeast on the way to China and Japan.
Most shops and schools were shut across Taiwan, hundreds of flights were cancelled and more than 4,300 people were evacuated from their homes ahead of the fierce storm.
One person has been killed in Taiwan after being swept away by waves whipped up by the typhoon, authorities said. At least 350 people have been injured.
"From tonight through tomorrow morning conditions will be very windy and stormy everywhere," Central Weather Administration (CWA) forecaster Ling Ping-yu told a briefing.
"Please try to stay indoors during this period for your safety."
Government text messages sent as Champi buffeted northern Taiwan Friday night warned of "destructive winds" and urged people to "take shelter ASAP."
Champi is the latest in a busy Pacific storm season turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.
The storm was briefly a super typhoon as it crossed the ocean, with reported maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 300 kilometres (186 miles) per hour, but has since weakened.
It gathered strength as it neared Taiwan on Friday afternoon and now has maximum speeds of 185 kph, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.
Thousands of military personnel are on standby to assist with rescue efforts, and authorities are racing to restore power to more than 21,000 households.
"As it approaches Taiwan's northeastern tip... the typhoon may slow down. If it slows down, its impact will last longer," CWA's Lu Kuo-chen said.
Stores were closed on Japan's southwestern island of Ishigaki, near Taiwan, and business owners draped windproof nets over their shops in an attempt to protect them from the strong winds.
Some tourists were also stranded due to flight cancellations, with many sheltering inside hotels.
"Lot of shops and restaurants were still open yesterday, and I could stock up on food, but there's not much information online about the typhoon and what to do," said Laura Czypulovski, 33, who lives in Zurich.
"It is now a pain to get back home – especially because it impacts my following flights, and then it caused a lot of rebooking."
Professional storm-chaser James Reynolds posted a video on X from Ishigaki showing a "fierce storm tide" in a channel leading to the island's harbour as Champi's strong winds whipped across the water.
"I'm seeing the ocean do things I've not seen in 20 years of doing this!!" Reynolds said in the post.
'Extremely heavy rain'
Champi is expected to dump up to 90 centimetres (35 inches) of rain from Thursday to Saturday, with northeastern Taiwan to be hardest hit, the forecaster said.
More than 40 centimetres of rain was recorded in Yilan county on Friday.
"People should be aware that the strong winds and extremely heavy rain will continue into the first half of tomorrow," the CWA's Lu said.
Work and classes were cancelled for the day across nearly all of Taiwan, leaving streets quiet as most locals hunkered down at home. The stock exchange was also closed.
"I'm worried about flooding. The vegetables could get flooded and rot," a 73-year-old farmer surnamed Tsai told AFP in New Taipei City.
Convenience store worker Peter Chen said he was concerned about the weather conditions on Friday night when the eye of the typhoon would be closer to Taiwan's coast.
"We might prepare some sandbags," the 27-year-old said.
The United Nations said Wednesday that the El Nino system gripping the planet is heading off the charts and that countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is expected to peak in December, but the human impact is set to last into 2027 and beyond.
The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding and exacerbate human-caused global warming. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
Article:
NAIROBI: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, with many feared trapped in the rubble and accusations of dangerous building work.
Videos shared online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building – thought to have been around 18 storeys high – came down in the densely populated business and residential area of Eastleigh.
The building was reduced to a pile of rubble as search and rescue teams arrived on the scene, but struggled to start accessing the site which was jammed between other high-rise buildings.
Police said they had already rescued one woman from the rubble, and could hear the voice of another.
"There are lots of people trapped here," Bibiye Mahmoud, president of the Institution of Engineering Technology of Kenya, told AFP at the site of the disaster.
"The contractors and the engineers are supposed to ensure that the works are followed by professionals. But most are not. This is why we are seeing these catastrophes... There is no accountability," she added.
Kenya's National Building Inspectorate report found that 87 per cent of buildings audited nationwide last year failed to meet standards or lacked the required approvals.
"Our concern is to save lives," Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja told reporters, adding: "This building has no occupation certificate...this has potentially cost lives."
An occupation certificate is essentially the authority's formal sign-off that a building is safe and legally fit to be occupied.
John Ogallo, vice-president of the Institution of Engineers of Kenya, who was also at the site, said there were warning signs about the building.
"People here are saying distresses were observed, like cracks," before it collapsed, he told reporters.
If you build with the wrong materials, "it becomes a time bomb," he added.
Nairobi is undergoing a rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city, particularly in Eastleigh which is known for its busy market areas and as a hub for the Somali community.
Local media reported looting immediately after the collapse, which happened around lunchtime. AFP saw police use tear gas to disperse crowds gathering near the site.
There have been many concerns over safety over the years.
There were 86 building collapses between 2009 and 2019 in Nairobi, killing an estimated 200 people, according to a report by the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis.
The number of buildings completed annually in Nairobi has risen from 20,025 in 2022 to 25,090 last year, according to its statistics bureau, as East Africa's leading business hub sucks in people from rural areas and neighbouring countries.
Corruption has allowed contractors to cut corners or bypass regulations.
Five people were killed when a six-storey building collapsed in a town on the outskirts of Nairobi in September 2022.
In April 2016, 49 people were killed when a six-floor apartment building crumbled in the northeast of the capital after days of heavy rain caused floods and landslides.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN ready to use Pas logo if barred from using own in Melaka polls
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is prepared to contest the Nov 14 Melaka election using the Pas logo if it cannot use its own.
PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the coalition had no objection to contesting under either the PN logo or Pas' moon symbol.
"We will face the Melaka polls soon. If we cannot use the PN logo, we will use the Pas logo. We are ready and have no problem with that," he said.
Sanusi, who is also Pas central election director, was speaking at the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (HIMPAK) gathering here today.
Also present were Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Wawasan president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Sanusi welcomed the High Court's decision to grant PN a temporary stay against the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) suspension and deregistration of the coalition, saying it would allow PN to continue operating as a coalition pending a judicial review.
"Alhamdulillah, the court has granted a stay on the cancellation of PN's registration, which we consider unlawful. The court's decision gives PN room to continue functioning as a legitimate coalition," he said.
The High Court yesterday allowed PN's application to
stay
the RoS action pending the full disposal of its judicial review, but did not determine whether the deregistration was lawful.
The ruling came ahead of nomination day on Oct 31, with polling scheduled for Nov 14.
Sanusi said supporters of "penyatuan ummah" (Muslim unity) wanted cooperation among the parties to continue regardless of the logo used.
"In Kelantan and throughout the country, those who support Muslim unity want to see this cooperation continue, regardless of the logo used," he said.
He also expressed confidence in the electoral cooperation, claiming that the Muslim unity movement had previously helped defeat Pakatan Harapan (PH) in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
"Our cooperation under the banner of Muslim unity will bring down PH. All this will lead us into the 16th General Election as the government-in-waiting," he said.
The remarks come as PN's component parties prepare for the Melaka polls following the RoS decision to cancel the coalition's registration on Oct 20.

Title: Birthday plans cut short after boy, 7, falls to his death from PPR block
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A family's plans to celebrate a 7-year-old boy's birthday next week were shattered when he died after falling from the 10th floor of their home at the Sungai Melana Phase 2 People's Housing Project (PPR) in Tampoi here.
His mother, Norhidayah Yacob, 30, said the family had planned to celebrate Mohammad Adib Rizqy Mohammad Fauzi's birthday yesterday but had to postpone it because her husband, Mohammad Fauzi Zurin, 31, who works as a lorry attendant, had yet to receive his salary.
"We had planned to celebrate my son's birthday next Tuesday, as it is also my husband's birthday.
"However, we accept what has been decreed by Allah. My son also passed away on this blessed Friday," she said when met at the scene.
The housewife said she was tidying up the house when the incident occurred, while her husband was away at work.
She learnt of the incident after one of her son's friends informed her.
"At first, I thought my son's friend was joking. When I went out and looked down from upstairs, I saw my son on the ground floor.
"I rushed downstairs and trembled when I saw that he was no longer moving before calling my husband to tell him what had happened," she said.
The victim, a
Standard One pupil
at SK Tampoi Utama, fell from the 10th floor of the PPR block around 5.30pm.
His body was sent to Hospital Sultanah Aminah here for a post-mortem.

Title: Nga: Future cities must balance modern technology with heritage preservation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Future urban development must balance technological advancement with the preservation of national heritage and identity to create comfortable, sustainable and climate-resilient cities.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said traditional design principles could be combined with modern technology to build homes better suited to local conditions, including hot weather and flood risks.
"Building the cities of the future does not mean setting aside our heritage and history. Instead, traditional design wisdom can be combined with modern technology to create homes that are more comfortable and resilient to hot weather and flood risks," he said at the national-level World Habitat Day celebration here today.
Nga, who is also president of the UN-Habitat Assembly, cited traditional Malay houses as an example of architecture that could inspire modern housing development.
He said features such as raised structures, natural ventilation and verandas that foster neighbourhood ties deserved greater consideration in future housing plans.
He said the Housing and Local Government Ministry encouraged the development of affordable homes near public transport and employment centres to ease daily commutes and improve quality of life.
Housing plans should also consider access to jobs, basic amenities, green spaces and community services to ensure residents could afford their homes and enjoy a conducive living environment, he said.
"Under the Malaysia Madani framework, a home is not merely a commodity, but a basic necessity that forms the foundation of the people's well-being," he said.
Nga said Malaysia was also strengthening its commitment to energy-efficient and climate-responsive housing through the IPOH Accord, finalised at the Fourth Asean-China Ministerial Roundtable Conference on Housing (ACMROCH).
This year's World Habitat Day carries the national theme "The Future City I Want to Live In", reflecting aspirations for cities that account for climate change, cultural heritage, development experiences and Malaysia's diverse communities.
At the event, Nga presented the Malaysia 2026 Honorary Scroll Award and the MUF 2026 Future City Pilot Project Award in recognition of contributions to improving urban well-being.
World Habitat Day was designated by the United Nations General Assembly to raise awareness of everyone's right to adequate shelter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
