Title: PM tells Cabinet to pursue major policy shifts for a more resilient Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has highlighted the need for Cabinet members to look at major policy shifts required to strengthen national resilience in industry and the economy.
He said he had raised the matter with cabinet members earlier today, emphasising that Malaysia has the resources, human capital, discipline, and resilience.
Anwar said he remained optimistic that Malaysia could forge ahead as a great nation through continued efforts by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) and collaboration with industry.
He was speaking at the Majlis Anugerah Kecemerlangan Industri (AKI) 2026 at Menara MITI here yesterday.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government played a pivotal role in ensuring stability and confidently crafting economic and national policies.
He cited the New Industrial Master Plan, energy transition, and digital transformation, stressing that policy clarity must be matched by effective execution.
“And in most countries, they can introduce and come up with some impressive plans, but there is no certainty that you are able or you will be able to execute it effectively.
“So the role of not only bureaucracy, but more so the industrial players, is critical,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar urges Malaysian industry to modernise and compete globally
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Budget 2027 provides a comprehensive framework to empower young people by expanding access to quality job opportunities, industry-driven skills training and stronger social protection.
Perdana Fellows Alumni Association secretary-general Amir Izzwan Abu Hasan said the budget initiatives covered various key stages of youth development, helping young people build resilience in the face of current economic challenges.
He said one of the major initiatives that should be fully utilised was the RM8 billion allocation to strengthen the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) ecosystem, alongside access to 16,000 courses on the Coursera platform and 100,000 free subscriptions to artificial intelligence (AI) technology.
“These funds and facilities provide an excellent platform for young people to upskill and reskill, ensuring their skills meet current industry demands.
“The MADANI Talent Programme, which aims to create 30,000 high-quality job opportunities by 2027, also reflects the government’s emphasis on quality employment that offers progressive wages, social protection and clear career pathways,” he said when appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Darah Muda programme titled Budget 2027: How Much Will Youth Benefit? Tonight.
Elaborating further, Amir Izzwan said young people should also take full advantage of wage restructuring policies, particularly the increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000, scheduled to take effect in June 2027.
He also described the relaxed deferment terms for National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan repayments, along with discounts for consistent repayments, as much-needed financial relief that would help them manage their daily cash flow.
For gig economy workers, he said the expanded RM160 million support package and the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid should be fully utilised to cope with the rising cost of living.
He also suggested exploring additional initiatives, such as affordable rental housing near public transport facilities and the expansion of the My50 travel pass, to ease the daily financial burden on urban youth.
“If opportunities are available but young people themselves are not proactive in seizing them, they will go to waste. Young people must make the most of these opportunities to advance their careers and improve their standard of living,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police rescue month-old infant dumped under stairs in Kepong’s Desa Aman Puri
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A baby boy, believed to be about a month old, was found alive in a box under the staircase of an apartment block in Kepong Thursday.
Gombak Police chief ACP Ibrahim Husin said police received a report about the discovery from a man in his mid-30s at 9.14 am.
He said the baby was believed to have been abandoned by an unidentified individual under the staircase of Block 1, Desa Satu, Desa Aman Puri Apartment, Jalan Puri Kepong.

Title: Recalculating… TuJu app promises to find its way back by Nov 6
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The technical team of the TuJu Highway Navigation Application is currently carrying out recovery and improvement work, targeted to be completed by Nov 6 at the latest.
The TuJu management, in a statement, said that updates on the recovery work will be communicated through TuJu’s official channels, while other functions in the application can continue to be used as usual for now.
In this regard, TuJu apologises to users who have experienced disruptions in navigation functions over the past few days.
“We take the difficulties experienced seriously and appreciate the feedback and criticism from users regarding our service.
“Our priority is to ensure that the navigation function operates stably and smoothly again, and meets the travel needs of users,” the statement said yesterday.
The statement also said TuJu is grateful for the patience and support of the users, while every report and feedback helps them identify issues and implement the necessary improvements.
“We will continue to strive to meet user expectations so that TuJu becomes one of the best navigation applications prioritising the safety of Malaysian citizens’ data,” the statement read.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported to have encouraged the public to use TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), as an alternative for road navigation needs.
The alternative measure was proposed following the risk to information security and the movement data of the people due to the use of the Waze application, which is bound by the laws of the Israeli government. — Bernama

Title: Experts say all high-risk groups vulnerable to haze, including those with medical conditions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — While haze exposure poses health risks to the general population, high-risk groups such as children, older adults and pregnant women are more vulnerable to its effects.
However, medical and health experts say no single group among those considered high-risk is necessarily more vulnerable than others, with susceptibility depending on factors such as age, underlying medical conditions and the duration and intensity of exposure.
Those with chronic lung diseases and other medical conditions are also among those who need to take precautions against haze exposure.
How haze affects high-risk groups
Universiti Malaya Faculty of Medicine’s social and preventive medicine department public health medicine specialist Dr Bala Murali Sundram said there was no single group among those considered high-risk that was more vulnerable than others.
He told
Malay Mail
that young children with asthma, older adults with heart or lung diseases, and pregnant women with underlying medical conditions may be especially susceptible during haze episodes.
Dr Bala, who is also the department’s Occupational and Environmental Health senior medical lecturer, said the risks vary according to age, existing medical conditions, and the duration and intensity of exposure.
“Children, especially those below five years of age, are more susceptible because their lungs and immune systems are still developing. They also breathe more air relative to their body weight and may spend more time being physically active.
File picture of a mother helping her child put on a face mask. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
“Older adults, defined in Malaysia as individuals aged 60 years and above, face increased risks because of age-related physiological changes and the higher prevalence of chronic disease,” he said, adding that haze can aggravate asthma, respiratory and cardiovascular conditions, potentially increasing the risk of hospitalisation, heart attacks and even strokes.
Pregnant women are another high-risk group, with Dr Bala saying epidemiological evidence links exposure to air pollution during pregnancy to adverse birth outcomes.
He said these include preterm birth and low birth weight.
“However, the risk depends on the timing, intensity and duration of exposure, and a brief haze episode does not necessarily result in pregnancy complications,” he noted.
Respiratory conditions and other health risks
Pantai Hospital Batu Pahat consultant internal medicine specialist, gastroenterologist and hepatologist Dr Mohamed Amin Kader said there was usually no single test to confirm an illness caused by haze exposure.
He told
Malay Mail
that diagnosis was based on symptoms, exposure, the patient’s medical history, underlying health conditions and clinical findings.
General practitioner Dr Boo Cheng Hau said most haze-related cases, particularly among high-risk groups, involved respiratory problems.
The former Johor assemblyman said these included acute exacerbations of bronchial asthma among children and adults, as well as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease among older adults.
A woman wears a face mask as she walks along a street in Kuala Lumpur on October 19, 2026. — AFP pic
“In addition, there is the issue of related allergic reactions and nasal congestion due to allergic rhinitis,” he said when contacted by
Malay Mail
.
Dr Boo said children could face more serious long-term effects because they would be breathing toxic gases and polluted air over a much longer period if the haze problem persisted.
Medical specialist Dr Norafiza Mohd Yasin said children with bronchial asthma, chronic respiratory illnesses or primary immunodeficiency may face a higher risk of complications.
She told
Malay Mail
that those undergoing chemotherapy or recovering from it may also be more vulnerable if their immune systems were suppressed.
What in haze can affect your health?
Dr Norafiza highlighted the risks associated with exposure to fine particulate matter known as PM2.5.
“The PM2.5 particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and may enter the bloodstream, worsening respiratory and cardiovascular conditions,” she cautioned, adding that pregnant women should also take precautions, as exposure to PM2.5 has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth and low birth weight.
Dr Mohamed Amin said PM2.5 particles could penetrate deep into the lungs and contribute to lung infections and pneumonia among high-risk groups.
He said children, particularly those below two years old, were more vulnerable.
“As their lung capacities are not fully developed yet, the haze can also aggravate asthma and trigger worsening respiratory symptoms,” he said.
The World Health Organisation defines PM2.5 as a mixture of solid and liquid particles, with major components including sulphates, nitrates, ammonia, sodium chloride, black carbon, mineral dust and water.
It also notes that PM2.5 can originate from direct emissions as well as chemical reactions between gases in the atmosphere.
Taking the right precautions
With air quality reaching unhealthy levels, health and medical experts advise the public to take steps to reduce their exposure to haze.
These include:
Wearing an N95 respirator when going outdoors to reduce exposure.
Staying indoors as much as possible, limiting unnecessary outdoor activities and prolonged exposure.
Taking extra precautions to protect children, older adults, pregnant women and people with respiratory or heart conditions.
Monitoring air quality in their respective areas.

Title: Haze can irritate skin and eyes, not just lungs, experts warn
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Haze pushed air quality to hazardous levels in parts of the country this year, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) peaking at 519 in six areas of Sarawak on September 1.
Readings above 300 are classified as hazardous, while those recorded across parts of Peninsular Malaysia in October, including Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan and Johor, mostly ranged from 101 to 210, within the unhealthy category.
While haze is commonly associated with respiratory and cardiovascular problems, medical experts say it can also affect the skin and eyes.
How haze affects skin and eyes
Medical specialist Dr Norafiza Mohd Yasin said PM2.5 particles, which measure 2.5 microns in diameter, can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, as well as disrupt the skin’s natural barrier.
“When PM2.5 particles infiltrate the pores, they disrupt the skin’s natural barrier.
“This leads to increased sensitivity, dryness, and irritation, often triggering flare-ups of underlying conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, and acne,” she said when contacted by
Malay Mail
.
Dr Bala Murali Sundram, a public health medicine specialist at Universiti Malaya’s Faculty of Medicine, said pollutants deposited on exposed skin can contribute to oxidative stress, inflammation and damage to the skin barrier.
“This may cause itching, dryness and redness or aggravate existing conditions such as eczema and atopic dermatitis,” he explained.
Pantai Hospital Batu Pahat consultant internal medicine specialist, gastroenterologist and hepatologist Dr Mohamed Amin Kader said fine particles in haze can cause dry eyes, redness and a stinging sensation.
“This ultimately can cause eye infection such as conjunctivitis if left untreated,” he said when contacted by
Malay Mail
.
Dr Bala, who is also a senior medical lecturer in the department’s Occupational and Environmental Health unit, said airborne pollutants can disturb the tear film and irritate the surface of the eyes, causing redness, burning, stinging, watery eyes and dryness.
“Individuals with dry-eye disease, allergies or contact lens use may experience greater discomfort,” he said.
How to reduce exposure
Dr Norafiza advised people to reduce unnecessary outdoor activities, particularly when the API reaches unhealthy levels.
“Staying indoors and keeping indoor air clean are important preventive measures.
“When outdoor exposure is unavoidable, a properly fitted N95 respirator can help reduce the inhalation of fine particles, although it does not protect against gaseous pollutants,” she said, adding that respirator suitability should be considered carefully for children, pregnant women and people with underlying medical conditions.
She advised the public to seek medical attention if symptoms persist or worsen, particularly in cases of eye pain, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or worsening asthma symptoms.
“Ultimately, prevention is key. Monitoring air quality, reducing unnecessary outdoor exposure and taking appropriate precautions are essential to protecting vulnerable groups during haze episodes,” she said.
Dr Bala advised the public to minimise unnecessary outdoor exposure, particularly when the API exceeds 100, and to avoid rubbing irritated eyes.
Contact lens users exposed to irritating dust or particles should remove their lenses before rinsing their eyes with clean water or sterile saline, he said.
Dr Bala also advised against using harsh soaps, vigorous scrubbing and excessive washing, which may worsen skin irritation.
He recommended keeping windows closed during heavy haze and using suitable air filtration at home where available to maintain cleaner indoor air.

Title: MCMC investigates Facebook’s failure to block livestream of teacher attack in Kuching, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating Facebook’s failure to detect or block a livestream of an attack on a teacher in Kuching, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The Madani government spokesperson said he would leave it to MCMC to investigate the incident before making any further comments.
He said the failure of social media platforms to prevent the livestreaming of violent acts was not new, with similar incidents having occurred in several other countries.
“MCMC is currently investigating the matter. We have seen similar cases in other countries where platforms have failed to prevent violent acts from being livestreamed.
“So, I will leave it to MCMC to investigate and issue a statement in due course,” he told a press conference here today.
He was responding to a question on whether the government had sought an explanation from Meta over Facebook’s failure to detect or block the livestream from the outset.
On Wednesday, a 16-year-old male student allegedly attacked a female teacher with an axe at an international school in Kuching, leaving the victim with injuries to her hand.
Sarawak Acting Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said the case was being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi tells LLM, Prosignal to explain TuJu app glitches and fixes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd have been asked to provide a detailed explanation of problems affecting users of the local navigation app TuJu, including their causes, technical issues and corrective measures.
Madani Government spokesman and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said LLM had acknowledged the problems and confirmed that improvements were under way.
“The explanation from LLM and Prosignal is crucial to addressing users' concerns comprehensively, improving TuJu's reliability and strengthening public confidence in the local navigation app,” he told a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today.
Fahmi also encouraged the public to consider alternative navigation apps developed by both local and foreign companies.
“What matters is avoiding Waze due to the security concerns highlighted by the National Security Council,” he said.
Last Tuesday, the government encouraged Malaysians to use TuJu, developed by LLM, as an alternative navigation app.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the recommendation followed concerns over information security and users' movement data, citing Waze's links to Israeli law.
TuJu was developed by Prosignal Consortium under a memorandum of understanding signed with LLM on May 26, 2022, and officially launched on November 26, 2025. — Bernama

Title: Anwar apologises over Waze ban linked to Israel, says national security comes first (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised if the decision to ban a navigation application owned by an entity linked to the Israeli regime causes any inconvenience to the public.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said this firm measure had to be taken to ensure the security of the nation and its people, a matter that cannot be compromised under any circumstances.
“I apologise if the decision to ban this navigation application, which belongs to the Israeli regime, causes inconvenience to the public.
“However, the security of the nation and its people cannot be compromised, as we must uphold national sovereignty and protect the personal information of our citizens,” he said.
Earlier, the prime minister indicated that the government has not ruled out the possibility of a complete ban on the use of the navigation application Waze in Malaysia.
He noted that such a move could be considered once the government has evaluated alternatives to Waze, including the potential for local development of a similar, fully functional application.

Title: Abang Johari: Some GPS incumbents willing to make way for new faces in Sarawak polls
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 23 — Some incumbent Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) assemblymen have indicated they are willing to make way for new candidates in the coming state election, said Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.
He said the coalition’s line-up would comprise a mix of experienced and younger leaders, with new faces expected to feature.
“It is not that they have been dropped, but some have decided to withdraw,” he told reporters at Kompleks Satria Pertiwi here today.
Abang Johari said the final decision on the candidates would be made at a GPS meeting, adding that the proportion of new faces had yet to be determined.
He also appeared to signal that he would defend his Gedong seat when asked by reporters, responding: “Gine fikir kitak (What do you think)?”
Earlier, Abang Johari announced that the Sarawak Legislative Assembly (DUN) would be dissolved on October 26 to pave the way for the next state election.
He said the announcement put an end to months of speculation over the timing of the dissolution.
The 82-member DUN currently comprises 79 GPS assemblymen, two DAP representatives and one independent assemblyman aligned with the ruling coalition.
The next state election will be held based on the existing 82-seat composition, as the proposed expansion of the DUN to 99 seats through the addition of 17 constituencies will not be implemented in time for the polls.
The Election Commission will announce the election timetable, including the nomination and polling dates. — The Borneo Post

Title: Female tapir killed in suspected collision on LPT2 near Kijal
Article:
CHUKAI, Oct 23 — An adult female tapir was found dead after it was believed to have been hit by a four-wheel-drive vehicle at KM 299.5 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), near Kijal here, this morning.
Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the department received information about the incident from the LPT2 management at 8am before four officers from the Kemaman district office were dispatched to the scene an hour later to investigate and conduct an inspection.
He said the inspection found that the 200-kilogramme tapir suffered head injuries, several abrasions on its body and a fractured left hind leg, believed to have been caused by the collision.
“The tapir carcass was disposed of after the inspection was completed,” he said in a statement today.
Dennis said the Bukit Kambing Forest Reserve was the nearest forest reserve to the scene, located about seven kilometres from where the tapir was found.
He also advised highway users to observe speed limits and pay attention to wildlife crossing warning signs to prevent similar incidents from recurring. — Bernama

Title: Federal Court to hear Negeri Sembilan exco members’ dismissal challenge on Dec 16
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Federal Court has set December 16 to hear the legal bid filed by ten deposed Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco) members to challenge the state ruler’s decision last month to revoke their appointments.
Lawyer Datuk Wira Mohd Hafarizam Harun, representing the former exco members, and lawyer Marisa Regina Mohd Aris Rizal, appearing for the Negeri Sembilan government, confirmed the hearing date when contacted by Bernama after case management Deputy Registrar Azaraorni Abd Rahman.
The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
They filed the notice of motion on October 14 and named the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary and the State Government as respondents.
Through the notice of motion, they are requesting that the court determine three legal questions concerning the effect and interpretation of provisions within the 1959 State Constitution of Negeri Sembilan — questions that have arisen from an originating summons they filed at the Seremban High Court.
On October 5, they filed an originating summons at the Seremban High Court to challenge the validity of the gazette notification revoking their appointments as members of the Negeri Sembilan State Exco.
One of the questions is whether Article 38(5), when read together with Articles 38(2), 38(3), 38(4), 40(1), 40(1A), and 40(2) of the State Constitution of Negeri Sembilan, authorises the Yang Dipertuan Besar to revoke the appointment of an Exco member without the advice of the Menteri Besar.
Should the answer to that question be in the negative, they seek a determination as to whether the revocation of the Exco appointments, as gazetted on September 24, was carried out in accordance with the State Constitution of Negeri Sembilan, and whether such revocation is null, void, and of no legal effect.
Another question is whether Article 38(5), read together with Article 28(1) of the State Constitution, implies that the term Raja Pemerintah (Ruler) refers to the Yang Dipertuan Besar, vesting him with the authority to revoke the appointment of an Exco member at his own discretion, without the advice of the Menteri Besar.
If the answer to this question is in the negative, then it must be determined whether their dismissal is contrary to the State Constitution.
On September 20, the Negeri Sembilan Palace announced that the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had revoked the appointments of the 10 Exco members with immediate effect.
The revocation of their appointments was gazetted on September 24, with their removal taking effect on September 20.
The gazette stated that their appointments were revoked and annulled because they violated their pledge of allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz when they agreed on Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as the Yang Dipertuan Besar. — Bernama

Title: ‘Completely false’: Waze rejects Malaysia’s data security claims after civil servant ban
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Navigation app Waze rejected on Friday Malaysia’s allegations that it could exploit users’ personal data, after the country banned civil servants from using the app over its Israeli links.
Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the ban on Wednesday to “safeguard government information and users’ personal data against the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime”.
He said Friday that the South-east Asian nation could consider a total ban if an alternative for the popular app is found.
Muslim-majority Malaysia is a longstanding and vocal critic of Israel and maintains no diplomatic relations with it.
Waze, owned by Google, was founded in Israel and remains incorporated there.
“Claims that Waze collects sensitive government information or allows any entity to exploit personal user data are completely false,” a Waze spokesperson told AFP in a statement.
“Waze operates under strict privacy policies that protect user data and comply with global legal data protection standards,” the statement read.
Anwar told reporters that Malaysia needed to look into alternatives to Waze, adding that if “our capabilities are good enough in the future, we may consider banning it altogether”.
“Our decision is not controversial,” the Malaysian leader said, adding that Malaysia was “being monitored” because of its opposition to Israel.
“They will use all their influence to go against us,” Anwar said, calling the issue “a matter of national security”.
Malaysia’s Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo told parliament on Thursday that the ban applied only to civil servants carrying out official duties.
He cited data security and legal concerns for the move, as “user data falls under Israeli jurisdiction”.
The government did not provide further details on the reason for the ban or how it would be enforced or monitored.
Malaysia’s National Security Council warned on Thursday that civil servants who defy the immediate ban “could face disciplinary action”.
Anwar suggested on Wednesday that users of Waze — which uses driver data to provide real-time traffic information — switch to platforms such as TuJu, a locally developed Malaysian road navigation app.
Waze is widely used in Malaysia, including as a back-up navigation aid by drivers for its Grab online cab-hailing service.
Many Malaysians complained that the TuJu app was “ineffective and should not be made a compulsory replacement for Waze”, former finance minister and MP, Lim Guan Eng, said. — Bernama

Title: Ready for floods and extreme heat? North-east monsoon begins Oct 27, MetMalaysia warns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL) is expected to begin on October 27 and continue until March next year, according to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip.
He said between three and five episodes of continuous heavy rain were expected to affect the country during the initial phase of the monsoon, from November to January.
He said the situation could lead to flooding in low-lying areas and locations near rivers.
“Continuous strong north-easterly winds could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea,” he said in a media statement today.
As the monsoon enters its final phase, from January to March 2027, Mohd Hisham said rainfall was expected to decrease, particularly in the northern states of Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah.
He said the conditions would bring hot, dry weather, with the potential for more extreme heatwaves due to the ongoing Super El Niño phenomenon.
In this regard, he advised the public to remain prepared for weather conditions throughout the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon and to stay alert to weather information, advisories, forecasts and warnings issued by MetMalaysia.
Official information is available via www.met.gov.my, the myCuaca mobile application, MetMalaysia’s official social media channels or its hotline at 1-300-22-1638. — Bernama

Title: Queen concerned over worsening mental health issues among children, teens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern over the worsening mental health issues among children and adolescents, which have led to loss of life.
The Queen’s concern for young people’s mental and emotional well-being has prompted Istana Negara to take proactive measures, including discussions on initiatives to develop and enhance complaint and counselling systems, according to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook page today.
This effort is specifically aimed at helping teens facing emotional distress, mental health problems and various life challenges.
Istana Negara Grand Chamberlain Datuk Azuan Effendy Zairakithnaini led the discussion, which brought together several government agencies, including the Education Ministry, the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry, the Communications Ministry, the Royal Malaysia Police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
“The discussion focused on strengthening accessible, safe and effective complaint and support channels, while improving the support available to students who require assistance,” the post said.
Persatuan Kaunseling Malaysia (Perkama International), an official association for the counseling profession and practice, will also work closely with the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry to involve counsellors registered with and trained by the Malaysian Board of Counsellors.
In the post, the Queen said the mental health of children and adolescents must be prioritised because they need to know that they are loved.
“It is our collective responsibility, regardless of our rank, position or occupation, to safeguard their physical and mental health and pay attention to their emotional well-being, whether at home or at school.
“Awareness of the importance of mental health must continue to be raised so that signs of emotional distress can be identified early and appropriate assistance provided,” Her Majesty said. — Bernama

Title: PTPTN sets RM50 minimum monthly repayment for graduates earning RM2,501 to RM3,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Graduates earning between RM2,501 and RM3,000 a month will only need to repay their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans at a minimum rate of RM50 per month, with the flexibility announced in Budget 2027.
Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim said the loan repayment flexibility initiative is expected to benefit more than 400,000 people, helping to ease the financial burden on graduates who have just entered the workforce.
He said graduates earning below RM2,500 a month would not need to begin repaying their loans until they reached the stipulated income threshold.
“We can address this concern in the most effective way possible for now.
“This is something that has been discussed and debated for years, and now, insya-Allah, we can implement it through Budget 2027,” he said in an interview with a local radio station recently.
Commenting on the cost of living among university students, Adam Adli said the Dapur Siswa Madani initiative, which provides centralised cooking facilities on campuses, would be expanded to polytechnics and teacher education institutes (IPGs) next year.
He said an allocation of RM20 million has been provided to supply food items and necessities, including rice, cooking oil, eggs and sardines, to the kitchens.
“Students can use the supplies to cook for themselves or in groups, with planning carried out together with student associations or kitchen managers to help control food expenses,” he said.
On transportation, he said the My50 pass would continue, in addition to the introduction of MyKomuter50 for users of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) commuter services, which students could also use for their daily journeys.
Meanwhile, he said the FlySiswa assistance would be increased from RM400 to RM500 annually for each eligible student to purchase flight tickets between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak for study-related travel.
At the same time, Adam Adli said the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) would continue to be strengthened for young people with an interest in technical skills, with the employability rate of its graduates standing at between 95 and 97 per cent annually.
He said investments in high-technology industries have also created job opportunities and demand for workers equipped with new skills.
As an example, he recounted meeting a polytechnic diploma graduate in his 20s who earned between RM6,000 and RM7,000 a month after working in a data centre in Johor for about a year following graduation.
“TVET is a pathway that we are strengthening to ensure that more young people, including school leavers who are not interested in academics but prefer technical disciplines, have an option that suits them. TVET is the answer.
“Sometimes, all we need is the skill,” he said. — Bernama

Title: RoS challenges court stay on Perikatan deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has filed an appeal against the High Court’s decision allowing Perikatan Nasional (PN) to suspend action by RoS to deregister the political coalition.
According to documents obtained by the media, Federal Counsel representing RoS director-general Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail filed the notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal today, following their dissatisfaction with the decision delivered by High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad yesterday.
Judge Azizan also allowed PN’s application to stay the implementation of RoS’ notice suspending all activities of the political coalition pending the court’s decision on its application for judicial review.
The decision paves the way for PN to contest the Melaka state election, scheduled for Nov 14.
Meanwhile, lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, representing the coalition, confirmed the filing of the notice of appeal.
On Oct 13, the court dismissed PN’s application for an interim stay of the RoS suspension notice but granted the political coalition leave to initiate judicial review proceedings.
The judicial review application was filed on Oct 5 by PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, together with Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerakan) secretary-general Wong Chia Zhen, Malaysian Indian People Party (MIPP) secretary-general N. Sathes Kumar, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) secretary-general Datuk Sazmi Miah, named as the first to fifth applicants respectively.
RoS had earlier issued an order suspending all PN activities with effect from Sept 23. According to an RoS statement, the action was taken under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966, following a notice issued to PN on Sept 22.
In their application, the applicants claimed that the suspension prevented them from carrying out their political activities as usual, including using the coalition’s name and symbol to contest the 16th Melaka state election.
Among other things, the applicants sought a certiorari order to quash the suspension order and the notice proposing PN’s deregistration.
On Oct 20, RoS deregistered PN under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 after finding that the coalition’s explanation had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration set out in the notice dated Sept 22. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Perikatan seat talks with Umno to be finalised within days, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 23 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is still negotiating to finalise seat allocations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition seeking one or two more seats on top of the seven discussed with Umno so far.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said talks were ongoing, and a final decision, including on any additional seats, was expected soon.
He said the discussions were now at the main committee level and would be finalised at a meeting expected within the next day or two.
“So far it is not final. Although the seven seats mentioned by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi are seats not won by Barisan Nasional (BN), we are still negotiating for one or two more seats.
“We expect it could be finalised today or tomorrow, God willing,” he told a press conference here today, Sinar Harian reported.
He was speaking after delivering a talk at the Kuliah Pagi Jumaat Perdana, held in conjunction with the Karnival Rakyat 36 Tahun Membangun Bersama Islam at Dataran Warisan, Stadium Sultan Muhammad IV.
Tuan Ibrahim said Umno had so far regarded the seven seats as those to be retained under the arrangement, but PAS hoped further talks would open the way for additional seats.
He said the final decision on seat allocation would be made by the parties’ top leadership through the seat negotiation committee.
On the seven seats under discussion, he said they comprised four seats won by DAP and three Malay-majority constituencies.

Title: Malaysia keeps Indonesia firefighting aid offer open, no local companies linked to forest fires
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysia’s offer to help Indonesia tackle forest fires causing transboundary haze remains open, with the government ready to provide firefighting assets if needed, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the Foreign Ministry and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) had yet to receive a full response from Indonesia on the type of assistance it was prepared to accept.
“The offer still stands. Malaysia remains ready to provide assistance and assets if required,” he told his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Fahmi said the Prime Minister had expressed appreciation for the strong diplomatic ties between Malaysia and Indonesia and reaffirmed Malaysia’s willingness to assist in efforts to put out the fires.
He said the Cabinet had also been briefed on the haze situation by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister.
Fahmi added that the Cabinet had been informed of an announcement by Indonesian authorities this morning that 11 companies had been subjected to action over the issue.
However, no Malaysian companies had so far been identified as being involved in forest-burning activities in Indonesia, he said.
The haze affecting Malaysia has been linked to smoke drifting across national borders from fires in neighbouring Indonesia, raising concerns over air quality, particularly in parts of the Klang Valley.

Title: Plan your commute: Severe weather warning for KL, Selangor, and nine other states this evening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6 pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather conditions in Peninsular Malaysia would affect the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as the whole of Perlis, Terengganu and Selangor.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling, while in Perak, they are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, while in Pahang, it covers Pekan, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Lipis, Jerantut, Temerloh and Maran.
The same warning has also been issued for Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan, and the Johor districts of Kluang, Mersing, Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat, Kulai, Johor Bahru and Pontian.
In Sarawak, the weather conditions are expected to affect Samarahan, Mukah (Matu, Dalat and Mukah), Sibu, Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh), Limbang, Miri (Marudi, Telang Usan and Beleru), Sarikei (Maradong), Kuching (Kuching and Bau) and Serian.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior (Pensiangan, Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu and Beaufort), Tawau, Sandakan and the West Coast (Ranau and Kota Belud). — Bernama

Title: Corporate mafia task force’s terms of reference to go before Cabinet next week, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The terms of reference for a special task force investigating allegations of a “corporate mafia” will be presented to the Cabinet next week, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the task force’s findings would be made public within three months of the completion of the investigation, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement in Parliament earlier this week.
“The Prime Minister also informed the Cabinet that the terms of reference for the special task force that will investigate the findings related to the corporate mafia issue will be presented at next week’s Cabinet meeting,” Fahmi said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Anwar said in Parliament on Tuesday that he had instructed a special task force led by the Attorney General to finalise its investigation and publicly disclose its findings within three months.
The investigation follows allegations of a purported “corporate mafia” reported by Bloomberg, which cited dozens of unnamed sources, including individuals purported to be serving Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and police officers.
The reports alleged that a group had plotted hostile takeovers of companies linked to projects awarded through government tenders.

Title: UK-based Malaysian lawyer named Multilaw chair-elect
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian lawyer Joanne Vengadesan has made history after being elected chair of Multilaw, a global network of law firms spanning over 100 countries with 300 offices.
The United Kingdom-based practitioner, who has 25 years of legal experience, was elected at Multilaw’s Global Conference in Prague earlier this month. She will serve a two-year term starting in September 2027, succeeding Australian lawyer Paul Kirton.
She began her career when she was called to the Malaysian Bar as an Advocate and Solicitor in 1997, initially practising intellectual property law in Kuala Lumpur.
Currently a partner at leading international firm Penningtons Manches Cooper LLP, Joanne is the daughter of retired Malaysian diplomat Datuk R. Vengadesan, who served as the country’s ambassador to several nations, including Italy and Namibia.
In a statement, Joanne said it was an honour to be named chair-elect, and she looks forward to taking on the role of chair next year.
“I love the perspective that being a Malaysian and working in the UK gives me. Malaysia is so multicultural that we grow up being so comfortable and at home with all our communities and cultures,” she said.
Joanne said her international upbringing played a significant role in fostering her interest in being part of a global legal community such as Multilaw. Her legal practice in the UK regularly handled cross-border matters.
“Multilaw has played a huge role in my career, and I am excited about the new challenges and opportunities to come. I could not be more proud of this network, which continues to go from strength to strength.
“The depth of the relationships and layers of connections between Multilaw member firms enable us to leverage the significant trust between us for the benefit of our respective clients. I am also very proud of my firm, Penningtons Manches Cooper’s, continued commitment and active engagement across the network,” she said.
Meanwhile, Penningtons Manches Cooper LLP chief executive officer Helen Drayton said she was pleased and proud of Joanne’s appointment, describing it as a testament to her talent, dedication and close collaboration with colleagues across the firm and the Multilaw network.
Multilaw chief executive officer Adam Cooke, who has known Joanne for nearly 20 years, said he had witnessed first-hand her energy, insight and warmth, adding that she understood the network’s emphasis on strong relationships, mutual trust and shared ambitions for its member firms and their clients. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi says Malaysians can use any navigation app except Waze, including overseas alternatives
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysians are free to use any navigation application other than Waze, including alternatives developed locally or overseas, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the government was not directing the public towards a single alternative amid concerns over Waze’s data security and ongoing efforts to improve the locally developed TuJu application.
“The government encourages the use of various applications. There are various alternatives, both locally developed and those from overseas.
“What is important is that Waze is not used, due to security concerns that have been communicated by the National Security Council,” he said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
“We are not directing everyone towards a single application. People can use various alternative navigation applications other than Waze,” he added.
Fahmi said the concerns over Waze were based on feedback from the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), which was conveyed to the National Security Council (MKN) and subsequently discussed by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN).
He said two key issues had been raised: the transfer of data collected and processed through the application to Israel, and the fact that any legal disputes would have to be handled through Israeli courts.
“Any legal disputes would be handled exclusively through the courts in Israel. This means that if any issues arise, we would not be able to pursue them there because Malaysia does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with it,” he said.
On TuJu, Fahmi said the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) had acknowledged the problems reported by users and was working to improve the application.
However, he said LLM and its developer, ProSignal Konsortium Sdn Bhd, needed to provide detailed explanations of the technical problems, the application’s current performance and the measures being taken to address users’ complaints.
He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar had been asked to coordinate a meeting involving the secretaries-general of several ministries to examine the use of navigation applications, including local alternatives, and ensure Waze was no longer used, particularly by civil servants.
The meeting would also examine explanations from LLM and ProSignal Konsortium, as well as TuJu’s functionality, user experience and improvement plans, including clear targets and timelines.
The ban on Waze was decided at a JKSN meeting, with Shamsul Azri instructing department heads to ensure it was implemented immediately.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that the government was looking into security risks arising from Waze, which he said was subject to Israeli laws.
Nacsa later clarified that the ban applied only to civil servants on official duty, although it encouraged them to uninstall Waze and switch to a local alternative.
LLM had apologised for disruptions to TuJu, attributing them to a surge in new users after Anwar’s call, while users also complained about its navigation and route accuracy.
Waze has rejected claims that it collects sensitive government information or allows any party to exploit users’ personal data, calling them false.

Title: BDS Malaysia backs civil service Waze ban, urges public boycott of navigation app
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — BDS Malaysia has welcomed the government’s directive banning civil servants from using Waze and its call for members of the public to stop using the navigation application.
In a statement today, the organisation said it supported the directive, citing concerns that the use of Waze could compromise Malaysia’s national security and sovereignty.
“We fully support this directive which is issued in the interest of preventing our national security and sovereignty from being compromised by Waze, an Israeli-based company, for the benefit of the Zionist apartheid and genocidal regime,” the statement read.
BDS Malaysia also urged the government to remain consistent in addressing national security concerns.
BDS Malaysia is part of the global Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, which campaigns for boycotts, divestment and sanctions against Israel in support of Palestinian rights.
On Wednesday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered civil servants to stop using Waze over concerns that sensitive government information and personal data could be exploited by Israel. — Bernama

Title: Architect charged with molesting senior cop’s son at Melawati gym sauna
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — An architect pleaded not guilty in the Ampang Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Taman Melawati last Sunday.
Datuk Saiful Anuar Abdul Aziz, 61, is accused of using criminal force against the 18-year-old victim with intent to outrage his modesty in a sauna room at a gymnasium in a shopping mall in Taman Melawati at 7.10 pm on Oct 18.
The charge, framed under Section 354 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum penalty of 10 years’ imprisonment, a fine or whipping, or any two of the punishments, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor M. Ramanathan Alias Ashwin proposed bail of RM15,000 with one surety and additional conditions that the accused not interfere with the victim or prosecution witnesses and surrender his passport to the court until the disposal of the case.
Counsel K. Theivaendran, representing the accused, sought a lower bail amount, saying his client was the family breadwinner and also supported his frail 89-year-old mother.
“I object to the prosecution’s application for my client to surrender his passport as he has projects abroad, including in Riyadh (in Saudi Arabia) and is not a flight risk,” he said.
Magistrate Siti Nur Ain Ariffin granted the accused bail of RM9,000 with one surety, imposed the additional conditions sought by the prosecution and fixed Nov 26 for mention.
Media reports last Wednesday said an elderly man had been arrested for allegedly molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Melawati.
The incident is believed to have occurred while the victim was at the gymnasium with a friend. — Bernama

Title: Abang Johari calls for Sarawak state assembly dissolution on Monday
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 23 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is set to be dissolved on Monday, Oct 26, 2026, paving the way for the 13th state election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution at a special press conference at the Satria Pertiwi Complex here this afternoon.
He said the decision was made after obtaining the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
“The governor has consented to my request to dissolve the Assembly in accordance with Article 21(2) of the Constitution of the State of Sarawak, with effect from Oct 26.
“Therefore, in accordance with Article 21(4) of the Constitution, the State Election must be held within 60 days from the date of the dissolution,” said Abang Johari.
Abang Johari, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman, said the Election Commission (EC) will be formally notified of the dissolution to enable the necessary arrangements to be made.
“During this period, the government will discharge its responsibilities in a caretaker capacity, observing the applicable constitutional requirements and conventions.
“Public administration and essential services will continue to ensure that the needs and welfare of the people remain attended to,” he said. — Bernama

Title: IGP: Police must treat seniors’ reprimands as lessons, not weakness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has reminded the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel to maintain discipline and respect for senior officers to preserve the force’s strength and harmony.
He said showing regard for senior officers appeared to be declining, raising concerns that this could weaken the police force and undermine its standing among other government departments and agencies.
“We know that observing the proper chain of command is essential. We must show respect to the seniors,” he said at the IGP’s monthly gathering organised by the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department at Bukit Aman here today.
Mohd Khalid also reminded members of the force to practise the discipline instilled during their training throughout their service, stressing that they should not regard being reprimanded by their officers as a negative experience, but instead take it as a lesson to improve themselves.
“Being corrected is not a wrongdoing in itself, but should serve as a lesson to help personnel recognise that a mistake has been made.
“We should not view being reprimanded as a sign of weakness…we should ensure the criticisms are constructive and help build character, enabling us to fulfill our duties and responsibilities with greater competence, discipline and integrity,” he said.
Mohd Khalid said police personnel should respect one another, accept feedback and different opinions, and recognise that they were not always right, adding that they should also remind one another of their responsibilities and respect senior officers to promote cooperation and solidarity within the force.
Meanwhile, Mohd Khalid said PDRM would celebrate Integrity Day on Nov 11 under the theme “Integriti dan Organisasi Bukan Pilihan Tetapi Kewajipan” (Integrity and Organisation: Not a Choice, but an Obligation).
He said the celebration would also honour 35 police personnel who had turned down bribes in the line of duty, recognising them as role models for their colleagues. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says nationwide Waze ban needs careful study first
Article:
AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today proposals for a nationwide ban on navigation app Waze required careful study, but did not rule out the possibility if capable local alternatives were available.
“It must be studied what are the alternatives first, and if we find that local capabilities are good enough then we may consider prohibiting Waze altogether,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers here.
Anwar again defended the ban on Waze for civil servants amid criticism, describing it as a crucial move to protect national security, even as he acknowledged that the decision had not been deliberated by the Cabinet beforehand.
“This is a heavy issue. When we checked Waze’s headquarters is in Israel, that’s one thing,” he said.
“Then a check showed Waze is governed only by Israeli laws. This is why I had to take a spontaneous decision because we cannot afford to delay even a single day…because all data are automatically handed to the Israeli government.”
